memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: As soon as they had brought them out, one of them said, "Flee for your lives! Don't look back, and don't stop anywhere in the plain! Flee to the mountains or you will be swept away!" - Gen 19:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once out of the city, the command is clear and urgent: "Flee for your lives! Don't look back, and don't stop!" There was no time to linger, no room for a backward glance, no safety in half-measures. To be rescued, they had to leave Sodom fully behind and press on to safety without hesitation.

"Don't look back" is more than practical advice about a collapsing city. It speaks to the heart. To look back is to long for what you are leaving, to let your affections remain in the place of death even as your feet move toward life. The command was for a wholehearted flight, not a reluctant, backward-glancing retreat.

There is a searching principle here for the life of faith. When God rescues us from something, He calls us to leave it fully behind - not to keep glancing over our shoulder, not to nurse a secret longing for what we've been saved from. Half-hearted escape, with the heart still turned backward, is dangerous.

Jesus said it starkly: "Remember Lot's wife!" (Luke 17:32) and "No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for service in the kingdom of God" (Luke 9:62). The call is forward - "straining toward what is ahead," pressing "toward the goal" (Phil 3:13-14). Whatever God has rescued you from, don't look back. Fix your eyes ahead, on Christ, and don't stop until you're safe in Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you still looking back at something God has rescued you from?
- What would it mean to flee wholeheartedly, without a backward glance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, when You rescue me, help me leave the old life fully behind, without a backward glance of longing. Fix my eyes ahead on You, and help me press on toward the goal without looking back.
Amen.
